item.title: The Prince's Virtue, East and West
item.description: Machiavelli's princes, the tyrants of Plato's dialogues and the emperors of China feign, sacrifice their ministers, destroy their captains and kill their kin with the same small repertoire, and they weep afterwards. What divides the three traditions is who may forgive the prince, and their words for his excellence, aretē, 德 (dé) and virtù, record the same choice. Since no prince can foresee the effect by which he asks to be judged, Machiavelli's excuse fails on its own terms.
